subject: Re-judge legacy kept edges with the validated neighborhood judge (shadow → apply)
description:
AFTER the judge-quality bench (eeadb38f-7472-4703-9689-fbf24eebee4d/1) shows the neighborhood-aware judge is accurate, re-judge the LEGACY kept edges (the ones promoted by the OLD endpoint-only judge, pre-task-A) with the validated judge, and clean the KB.

WHY now-blocked: re-judging is an ACTION that mutates the KB. The shadow re-judge measures decision CHANGE, not accuracy — a flip = the judges disagree, not that the new one is right. So this MUST wait until the bench (eeadb38f.../1) proves the neighborhood judge is accurate against ground truth; only then are the flips trustworthy.

SCOPE:
1. Identify the legacy population: edges currently judged:true that were judged in the ENDPOINT-ONLY era (before task A's neighborhood judge went live — use the verdict-journal timestamp / pre-activation epoch). Note: legacy PRUNED edges are deleted, so this can only re-judge the KEPT ones (measures keep→prune, i.e. did the old judge over-keep). prune→keep recovery needs re-running recall — out of scope here (separate pass).
2. SHADOW first: re-judge a sample with the neighborhood judge WITHOUT applying; record new verdict vs the journal's recorded verdict; report flip-rate + concrete examples (especially keep→prune flips the neighborhood context catches).
3. APPLY: only if the bench validated the judge, apply the flips (prune the false-keeps the neighborhood judge now rejects), journaling each as a verdict. Keep it reversible/auditable.
4. Report: flip-rate, how many false-keeps pruned, examples, and whether the neighborhood context (not endpoint-only) drove the flips.

CAVEAT: no ground truth here either — but the bench dependency means the judge is pre-validated, so applying flips is justified. Daemon restart not needed (runs against live judge). Blocked by eeadb38f.../1.
